body:
Merged `main` (8f30bee) into the branch to clear the conflict with #21's blade footprint in `crates/app/src/stock_sim.rs` (3ba842f). The resolution keeps both: a lathe plan's display radius is `LathePlan::feature` (main's change), and every other tool still sweeps `tool_law::cutting_radius` (a tap its thread's core, this PR).

Re-ran the quick gate's plan for this diff on the merge (app lib, `lathe_field_sim`, `lathe_field_tools`, `post_not_judged`, `posting`, `real_tip_contour`, `rotary_field_parity`, `stock_engine_agreement`, `stock_export`, `stock_field_cost`, `stock_sim_document`, `stock_view`, `tap_sim`, `tool_law`, `verify`): 162 pass, 7 ignored (ignored on `main` too). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Still a draft: the generator-verify half described on #266 needs the owner's call (core radius for the cutting laws only, and the tapped-hole convention in `solid_law_goldens.rs`).

Hi @austin62jake - thanks for this! This PR is still a **draft**, and drafts are not picked up for review: the review queue only takes PRs marked ready. When you're happy with it and its tests pass, please click **Ready for review** (or run `gh pr ready 271`), and it will get a full review - green `merge-ready` if clean, or a comment saying what to change. See the README's Contributing section, "Draft first, then ready for review: the gates".
Do you need help with this?

Hi @austin62jake, thanks for this. A pre-ready check on a local trial merge is **clean apart from one merge conflict**, so once you push the resolution below, this should be ready to flag. Nothing here was pushed to your branch; it's your PR and your call when to mark it ready.

## 1. Resolve the conflict with `main` (one hunk)

Since this branched, `main` added a `breaks:` field to the same `Planned { ... }` literal this PR edits. It conflicts in `crates/app/src/stock_sim.rs` only, inside `plan_program`'s `planned.push(Planned { ... })`.

```sh
# once, if your clone has no upstream remote yet
git remote add upstream https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft.git

git fetch upstream
git switch issue/266-tap-minor-sweep
git merge upstream/main
```

Git will stop with:

```
CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in crates/app/src/stock_sim.rs
```

The hunk looks like this:

```rust
<<<<<<< HEAD
            breaks: cache.path.breaks,
            // A turning insert's cutting feature is its nose (a
            // blade's, half its band - `LathePlan::feature`): the
            // display cell law (`auto_cell`) reads it, not the IC.
            radius: lathe.map_or(tool.diameter / 2.0, |l| l.feature()),
=======
            radius,
>>>>>>> upstream/main
```

(The side labels may be swapped depending on which branch you are on.)

**Keep both:** main's `breaks:` line and your `radius,`. Drop the old inline `radius: lathe.map_or(...)` line and its comment, since your `let radius = match lathe { ... }` above the push already covers the lathe case:

```rust
            breaks: cache.path.breaks,
            radius,
```

Then:

```sh
git add crates/app/src/stock_sim.rs
git commit --no-edit
```

## 2. Re-gate and push

```powershell
cargo test -p camcraft-app --test tap_sim
scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick
cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings
```

```sh
git push   # a plain push - never force-push a branch with an open PR
```

## 3. Mark it ready

Once it's pushed and green:

```sh
gh pr ready 271 --repo NeoTech/Camcraft
```

After that, the review loop (`/review-prs`) gives it the full review and the label: `merge-ready` if it's clean and mergeable. The maintainer merges it.

## What the trial merge showed

This was run on the merged tree, upstream `main` 66791aa6 plus this PR, on macOS:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `tap_sim` | 2 passed |
| `tool_law` | 4 passed |
| `stock_sim_document` | 9 passed |
| `stock_view` | 4 passed |
| `stock_play` | 7 passed |
| `post_not_judged` | 4 passed |
| `posting` | 17 passed |
| `operations` | 117 passed |
| `wall_column_gouge` | 3 passed |
| `real_tip_contour` | 4 passed |
| `contour_arc_sim` | 1 passed |
| `edge_break_gate` | 5 passed |
| `carried_verify` | 8 passed |
| `setup_carry` | 9 passed |
| `turning_thread` | 8 passed |
| app lib | 101 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |

So it also passes on macOS, which your body said wasn't run.

- **`cutting_radius` (`tool_law.rs`) checks out.** It uses ISO 724's `0.5413 x pitch`, the same constant as the thread mill. A pitch too coarse to leave a core is refused by name, every other tool still sweeps `d/2`, and a turning insert still uses its nose.
- **No gouge is hidden.** `a_tap_wider_than_its_hole_is_still_a_gouge` holds, and a tap over solid metal still gouges.
- **Merging it as a partial fix (`Refs #266`) is fine.** It changes no toolpath or posted G-code and loosens no safety law. The op's own verify still blocks the post until the follow-up, and the decision file says so.

**Non-blocking note:** a Tap-kind tool with `pitch = 0` gets a core of `d/2`, the old behaviour. It is harmless, but the maintainer may prefer refusing a zero-pitch tap. Worth a line on #266.

This PR closed itself when I pushed the conflict fix (6d2f134c). The close was not intended. The cause: `austin62jake/Camcraft` is no longer in this repo's fork network. GitHub now lists its parent as `linuxguy123/Camcraft`, which is itself no longer a fork. A cross-repo PR can't follow a head outside the base's network. For the same reason, a new PR from this fork is refused ("No commits between NeoTech:main and austin62jake:...").

State of the branch `austin62jake:issue/266-tap-minor-sweep` at 6d2f134c:
- upstream `main` b57f8d52 merged in. The one conflict, in `plan_program`'s `Planned { .. }`, was resolved as @mkinney described: main's `breaks: breaks::bounded(..)` plus this PR's `radius,`.
- Quick gate plan (`scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick -DryRun`) run on that head, Windows: app lib 102 passed. Also passed: `tap_sim` 2, `tool_law` 4, `posting` 17, `verify` 21 (+2 ignored), `edge_break_gate` 5, `edge_break_bound` 3, `stock_sim_document` 9, `post_not_judged` 4, `real_tip_contour` 4, `wall_column_gouge` 3, `lathe_field_sim` 6, `lathe_field_tools` 2, `carried_verify` 8, `carried_fixtures_cache` 6, `setup_align` 9, `setup_carry` 9, `setup_stock_source` 6, `rotary_field_parity` 3 (+1 ignored), `stock_view` 4, `stock_export` 2, `probe_only_sim` 2, `contour_arc_sim` 1. The ignored tests are ignored on main too.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` stops at `lathe_thread_travel`, which doesn't compile on main itself (#686). That file isn't part of this diff.

On the zero-pitch note: a Tap-kind tool with `pitch = 0` keeps the full `d/2` sweep. That is the old, wider sweep, so it can report a false gouge but never hide a real one.

**Update 2026-11-10:** re-opened as #713 from a new fork, `austin62jake/Camcraft2`: the same commits, plus `main` f42d3788 merged in (no conflicts).
